Introduction
A cabin fire far from Earth can't wait for mission control
On a space station, Moon base or Mars habitat, a fire can spread before anyone on Earth even hears the alarm. A signal from Mars takes over 12 minutes one way.
NASA’s fire experiments sit in dense abstracts. We turn them into evidence that crews and an autonomous agent can act on.
Our question: how much does each finding affect fire risk or fire response on a Moon or Mars spacecraft or habitat?
1 · Research dashboard
40 NASA fire experiments, scored 1–10 by AI and checked by our Science Lead.
Superintelligence
2 · Autonomous SI fire-safety agent
Always on: it watches the cabin sensors live and raises the alarm. Then it forecasts the fire and decides on its own, taking the right action based on NASA experiment data.
3 · Dynamic risk scoring & prediction
A live Fire Hazard Score (0–100) for 4 environments (space station in microgravity, Moon at 1/6 g, Mars at 3/8 g, Earth lab at 1 g), with a 60-second forecast.

Every decision is forecast, evidenced and logged
Contained, with evidence

Feature 2 · Memory, readiness & guardrails
It learns from each fire, within strict rules
Readiness & memory
  • Readiness 0–100 per environment and material; riskiest: space station + foam (62).
9 guardrails
  • No inert gas until the crew is clear; act only if it cuts damage by 15%; failed actions are logged and replaced.
Feature 3 · Dynamic risk scoring & prediction
Watching every cabin and predicting what's next
Live hazard score
  • Sensors feed a Fire Hazard Score (0–100); advisory at 55, alarm at 75.
60-second forecast
  • Projects each score a minute ahead and shows its own accuracy.
How the score is built
  • Rule-based: 40% oxygen and pressure, 20% airflow, 40% material.
Honest limits: sensor values are simulated, the fire model is illustrative, Moon and Mars scores are extrapolated, and nothing here controls real hardware.
